`src/Encina.ADO.SqlServer/Sagas/SagaStoreADO.cs:264-268`, `src/Encina.ADO.PostgreSQL/Sagas/SagaStoreADO.cs:266-270`, `src/Encina.ADO.MySQL/Sagas/SagaStoreADO.cs:266-270`: `OpenConnectionAsync` is `{ cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested(); return Task.CompletedTask; }` -- it never calls `.Open()` or `.OpenAsync()` on the connection. Every public method (`GetAsync`, `AddAsync`, `UpdateAsync`, `GetStuckSagasAsync`, `GetExpiredSagasAsync`) guards with `if (_connection.State != ConnectionState.Open) await OpenConnectionAsync(cancellationToken);` (lines 55-56, 94-95, 133-134, 171-172, 213-214 in the SqlServer file) and then proceeds to execute the command regardless. The production registration path hands this store a freshly constructed, closed connection (`services.AddEncinaADO(string connectionString, ...)` -> `_ => new SqlConnection(connectionString)`, `src/Encina.ADO.SqlServer/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:219`, never opened); nothing else opens it in the DI graph unless `config.UseTransactions = true` also registers `TransactionPipelineBehavior`. A consumer who enables `UseSagas` without `UseTransactions` -- a perfectly valid, documented combination -- gets `InvalidOperationException` on the very first saga call. This is masked in the integration test suite: `tests/Encina.TestInfrastructure/Fixtures/SqlServerFixture.cs:69-74`'s `CreateConnection()` calls the *synchronous* `connection.Open()` before handing the already-open connection straight to `new SagaStoreADO(...)` (`tests/Encina.IntegrationTests/ADO/SqlServer/Sagas/SagaStoreADOTests.cs:29`), so the broken branch never executes under test. Fails AGENTS.md paragraph "Database calls MUST be asynchronous with a `CancellationToken` (`OpenAsync`, ...); NEVER the synchronous overloads" -- here it is worse than a sync call, since the connection is never opened by any path at all in the store itself.
